---
title: "A function created in a loop forgets its value"
ref: FUN-04
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'f_1()'
reponse: '2'
attendu: "`1`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
for (i in 1:2) {
  assign(sprintf("f_%s", i), value = function() {
    i
  })
}
f_1()
```
:::

## Why

A function does not copy the variables it uses: it keeps a link to the environment where it was created, and looks up `i` there when it is called. A `for` loop has no environment of its own. Both functions therefore share the same `i`, which is 2 at the end of the loop.

## The fix

Create each function in its own environment, for example with `lapply()`, which calls a new function at each step.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
funs <- lapply(1:2, function(i) {
  function() {
    i
  }
})
funs[[1]]()
```
:::
